The current DD4hep/DDG4 runtime and Geant4 datasets are verified. The matched route is about 4.968 m long in both cases; the bend approximation will correct its small chord-length deficit without changing material density.

I’ll also check the routes against the existing ECAL. The proposed neck crosses closed vessel walls, so that fit check needs to remain distinct from validation of the standalone pipe shapes.

The fit check has identified an important detail: part of the common upstream route is already occupied by existing N₂ pipes. I’ll distinguish those continuation contacts from the new vessel penetrations, so a simple overlay cannot be mistaken for an extra, material-consistent cooling circuit.

Both standalone route models now construct successfully, with zero overlaps at the retained 10 nm tolerance. The native checks cover the steel/core material inventories and the joins between bend segments.

The Geant4 smoke test is checking saved steps through the wall, nitrogen core and miter joins. The separate ECAL diagnostic confirms that vessel penetrations and existing-pipe continuation still need integration work.

The clean committed candidate has passed the old/new native checks, a finer 2.5° construction check, and six saved Geant4 smoke events. The old/new steel and nitrogen inventories agree to numerical precision.

I’m packaging those results for review, with the context contacts reported separately from the standalone component checks.
